notes:
Inbound SMB trial sign-up (self-serve) from marketing team. Primary product interest: Hosted API for chat/support-bot and light embedding use. Topline complaint: slow response times when users in EU connect — average perceived reply latency 1.5-3s (not token-level) and occasional 10s+ spikes. CTO said: "UX suffers when chat takes >2s, conversion drops on checkout flows." They are cost-sensitive but willing to pay small premium for regional routing.

Observed from logs / user reports:
- Most traffic originates from EU (Dublin, Berlin) but account default region is us-west-2.
- One intern ran basic end-to-end test and saw 2.8s RTT to us-west, 160ms to us-east during one test (likely infra variance).
- Multiple requests hit 45s client timeout on long-context summarization tasks (max_tokens heavy).

What we recommended on call (high level):
- Switch default deployment region to eu-central-1 for EU customers or enable smart routing to nearest region. Quick win for perceived latency.
- Use streaming endpoints for chat to surface tokens asap (improves UX even if total completion time similar).
- Shorten prompt prefixes and use system templates with placeholders; move long contextual docs into embeddings + retrieval to reduce prompt length.
- Reduce max_tokens for assistant completions and rely on incremental prompts for long dialogs.
- Client-side: set conservative HTTP timeout (45s) and implement exponential backoff + idempotency keys for retries.
- Suggested model families: recommend smaller latency-optimized variants for high-volume chat (lower cost tier) and reserve larger models for batch reranking / nightly jobs.

Customer reaction: interested but wants simple checklist they can hand to front-end engineer. Also asked about SLA/uptime for hosted API and whether Redwood can do automated region fallback if a region is degraded.

Notes on procurement/security: submitted basic SOC2 checklist; they will need SSO via SAML and audit logs for compliance with their retail partners. Not planning private deployment right now — prefer public cloud due to time-to-market.

Short quote from Head of Eng: "If we can cut median UI latency to <1.2s and avoid those 10s+ spikes, we'll expand to more flows."
